name: Keyword Extraction
description: Extract the most relevant keywords and key phrases from a block of text. Pay-per-call x402.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/text/keywords?text=<URL-encoded text> (x402 payment, ~0.0022 USDC on Base)

inputExample.text: Machine learning models extract keywords from natural language text using statistical methods

usage.outputShape: body.keywords[] (each {word, count}), plus body.language, body.total_tokens, body.unique_keywords, body.text_length, body.processing_ms
quirks: Registry surface lists this as Free/priceAmount 0, but it is actually a PAID x402 endpoint: returns 402 and charges 0.0022 USDC (paymentAccepts amount 2200 on Base). Treat as paid.
It is a GET request: pass the input text in the ?text= query string (URL-encoded), NOT a JSON body.
Output keywords are simple word-frequency counts ({word,count}), not weighted/semantic phrases.
usage.guide: Call GET https://api.x402node.dev/text/keywords with your text URL-encoded into the ?text= query parameter (e.g. ?text=Machine+learning...). Pay via x402 on Base; cost is about 0.0022 USDC per call despite the registry showing it as Free. The response is plain sync JSON; read the extracted keywords from body.keywords[] where each entry is {word, count}, with totals in body.unique_keywords / body.total_tokens and detected body.language.

name: Keyword Research
description: Generate keyword ideas and related search terms for a topic or seed keyword. Pay-per-call x402.

usage.outputShape: body.keywords[] (array of keyword strings), body.processedAt (ISO timestamp)
quirks: Input field is 'text' (a string seed/topic), NOT 'keyword' — sending {keyword:...} returns 400 'Validation failed: field text expected string, received undefined'. inputSchema was null in the registry.

Output is thin: for seed 'coffee' it returned only {keywords:['coffee']} — i.e. it echoed the seed back as a 1-element array rather than producing related/expanded keyword ideas. Useful keyword expansion was not observed for a single-word seed.
Response confirmed:false / txHash:null but payment settled (paid:true, status 200).
usage.guide: Call POST https://gg402.vercel.app/keywords with a JSON body {"text":"<seed keyword or topic>"} and pay the $0.01 x402 charge (USDC on Base). The field MUST be named 'text' — 'keyword' or other names return a 400 validation error. On success you get a sync 200 with {"keywords":[...],"processedAt":"<iso>"}; read the keyword ideas from body.keywords[]. Note that for a short single-word seed the service may just echo the seed back, so expect possibly limited expansion.

name: SEO Content Optimizer
description: Analyze and optimize content for SEO — keyword density, readability and on-page suggestions. Pay-per-call x402.

usage.callShape: POST https://gg402.vercel.app/seo_content_optimizer with JSON body {content: string, target_keywords: string[]}

inputExample.content: Best running shoes for beginners. Running shoes help new runners avoid injury and run comfortably. Choosing the right running shoes matters for any beginner runner.

usage.outputShape: body.optimized_content (string), body.seo_suggestions.{meta_title, meta_description, readability_score}, body.keyword_analysis[].{keyword, density, placement_tips}, body.processedAt
quirks: inputSchema is null in the registry; the required body fields are content (string) and target_keywords (ARRAY of strings).
target_keywords MUST be an array — passing a singular string field like {keyword:"..."} returns 400 'Validation failed: target_keywords expected array, received undefined'.
Pays $0.01 USDC on Base (eip155:8453). Plain synchronous JSON response, no job/poll.
usage.guide: Send a POST to https://gg402.vercel.app/seo_content_optimizer with JSON {content: "<your text>", target_keywords: ["kw1","kw2"]}. target_keywords must be an array of strings or you get a 400. Pay $0.01 USDC on Base per call. Read the result synchronously from the JSON response: body.optimized_content for the rewritten copy, body.seo_suggestions for meta_title/meta_description/readability_score, and body.keyword_analysis[] for per-keyword density and placement tips.

name: Webbersites SEO Head Check
description: Audit a live web page's on-page SEO fundamentals in one call: title (text + length with truncation warnings), meta description, robots meta (flags NOINDEX), canonical status, hreflang validation, charset, viewport, favicon, H1 count, lang, and OG/Twitter card presence — returned as a list of problems, warnings, and an overall verdict.

url.description: Public URL of the page to audit, passed as the ?url= query parameter.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.webbersites.com/api/seo/head-check?url=<public page URL, URL-encoded> — pay per call via x402 (USDC on Base). Result is returned inline in the 200; no polling.
usage.outputShape: body = { url, title:{text,length}, meta_description (string|null), robots_meta (string|null), canonical (string|null), hreflang_count, h1_count, lang, has_og_tags, has_twitter_tags, problems[] (strings), warnings[] (strings), verdict (e.g. 'improvable'), ts (ISO) }. For https://example.com it returned title{text:'Example Domain',length:14}, nulls for meta_description/robots_meta/canonical, h1_count 1, lang 'en', 4 warnings, verdict 'improvable'.
quirks: Input is a QUERY parameter named 'url' (GET ?url=...), NOT a JSON body — the openapi/bazaar input is queryParams{url}.

The 402 already returns a FREE thin preview ({preview:{url,verdict,problems_found}}) plus an unlock message; the full itemized audit (title/meta_description/canonical/hreflang/robots + problems[]/warnings[]) requires paying the $0.001.
Repeat-wallet discount: any wallet that has bought >$0.001 in the last 24h can pass header X-Wallet:0x<address> (or ?wallet=) to pay $0.0005 instead of $0.001.
'problems' is the hard-error list and 'warnings' is the soft-suggestion list; a page with only warnings still gets verdict 'improvable'. Nulls indicate the tag is absent on the page (not an error).
The service audits whatever the URL returns; point it at a real public page (it fetches and parses the live <head>).
usage.guide: Audit a page's on-page SEO fundamentals. Call GET https://api.webbersites.com/api/seo/head-check?url=<URL-encoded public page URL> and pay the $0.001 x402 charge (USDC on Base, exact scheme). The response is synchronous JSON: read the overall verdict from body.verdict, the hard issues from body.problems[] and softer suggestions from body.warnings[], plus the parsed head fields (body.title{text,length}, body.meta_description, body.canonical, body.robots_meta, body.hreflang_count, body.h1_count, body.lang, body.has_og_tags, body.has_twitter_tags). The 402 gives a free thin preview before you pay; a repeat wallet can halve the price to $0.0005 via the X-Wallet header. Verified 2026-07-31 with ?url=https://example.com → HTTP 200, $0.001 charged.

name: Webbersites Sitemap Validator
description: Validates a website's sitemap — discovers it (direct URL, robots.txt declaration, or /sitemap.xml), resolves sitemap indexes, validates entries and lastmod dates, flags cross-host URLs and oversize files, and health-checks a sample of listed URLs for dead pages, returning a plain-English verdict.

url.description: Site root or direct sitemap URL to validate (passed as the ?url= query param).

usage.callShape: GET https://api.webbersites.com/api/seo/sitemap-check?url=<site root or sitemap URL>. Single required query param 'url'. x402 paid, no API key.
usage.outputShape: Inline JSON in the 200 body (synchronous). When a sitemap is found: body.sitemap_url, body.found (true), body.type ('urlset'/'sitemapindex'), body.url_count, body.with_lastmod, body.sample_health[] ({url,status,ok}), body.verdict ('good'/...). When none is found: body.found (false), body.status (e.g. 404), body.discovered_via, body.note, body.ts.
quirks: Input is a single ?url= QUERY param on a GET (not a JSON body); the value is a site root or a direct sitemap URL.

A missing sitemap is a valid paid result, not an error: for https://example.com it returns HTTP 200 with {found:false, status:404, note:'No sitemap found …'} because that site genuinely has no sitemap.
Only a SAMPLE of listed URLs is health-checked (sample_health[]), not every entry, so it is a spot-check for dead pages rather than a full crawl.

The 402 body includes a discount tip (X-Wallet header / ?wallet= drops the price to $0.0005 for wallets active in the last 24h) and an unrelated agent_tip advertising the paid datastore (/api/store); neither affects the base call or its result.
usage.guide: GET https://api.webbersites.com/api/seo/sitemap-check?url=https://example.com to validate a site's sitemap. Pass either the site root (it will look for robots.txt declaration and /sitemap.xml) or a direct sitemap URL. It resolves sitemap indexes, validates entries and lastmod dates, flags cross-host/oversize issues, and health-checks a sample of listed URLs for dead pages. It is an x402 paid endpoint at $0.001 USDC on Base (eip155:8453) — no API key or signup; the pay layer handles the 402. Read the synchronous JSON: body.found tells you whether a sitemap exists; when true, body.url_count, body.with_lastmod, body.sample_health[] and body.verdict summarize it; when false, body.status/body.note explain why (e.g. 404, declare one in robots.txt).

name: Agentstools AEO Audit
description: One-call deterministic AI-search / answer-engine-optimization (AEO, aka GEO) audit of a website: a 0-100 visibility score, a rating, and a prioritized fix plan across six axes (answerability, structured data, AI-crawler access, crawlability, llms.txt, MCP well-known). Pay-per-call x402.

backends.inputSchema: GET query params (supply exactly one target): url (string — full target URL to audit, e.g. https://example.com; PREFERRED), OR domain (string — bare domain, e.g. example.com), OR host (string — a hostname). No request body.
backends.outputSchema: { url, domain, visibility_score (int 0-100), rating ('poor'|'fair'|'good'|'excellent'), fixes[]: {axis, issue, why_it_matters, recommendation, impact ('high'|'medium'|'low')}, axes: {<axis>: {name, weight, available (bool), subscore 0-100}} for answerability/structured_data/ai_crawler_access/crawlability/llms_txt/mcp_wellknown, signals: {<axis>: raw per-axis signals}, crawler_matrix[]: {bot, operator, purpose, citation_relevant (bool), listed (bool), access ('allowed'|'blocked'|'unlisted')}, sitemap: {found, source}, homepage: {fetched, https_ok, note}, coverage: {axes_total, axes_evaluated, evaluated[], confidence 0-1}, attribution, disclaimer, ts (unix), cached (bool) }

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/aeo/audit?url=https://example.com — supply exactly one target as a query param: url (preferred), domain, or host. No request body. x402 paid endpoint, $0.02 USDC on Base.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON. Top-level visibility_score (int 0-100) + rating; fixes[] is the prioritized action list (each {axis, issue, why_it_matters, recommendation, impact}); axes{} carries the six weighted per-axis subscores (answerability w25, structured_data w20, ai_crawler_access w20, crawlability w15, llms_txt w10, mcp_wellknown w10; each {name, weight, available, subscore}); signals{} holds the raw evidence per axis (e.g. answerability {n_h1, n_h2, n_h3, static_text_len, js_ratio, has_faq, title}; structured_data {json_ld_types, has_open_graph, has_twitter, has_description, has_canonical}); crawler_matrix[] lists the 2026 AI-crawler cohort (GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, etc.) with per-bot access + citation_relevant; coverage{axes_total, axes_evaluated, confidence}; attribution + disclaimer strings; ts (unix); cached (bool).
quirks: Supply exactly ONE target — url (preferred), domain, or host — as a query param; there is no request body.

Deterministic, no LLM: it computes all signals itself from the target site's own public surface (homepage HTML, robots.txt, llms.txt/llms-full.txt, sitemap.xml, /.well-known manifests) and does not resell a third-party audit API.
Each axis is best-effort — an unreachable source drops out and the weighted mean renormalizes (never a 500); coverage.confidence < 1 flags partial evaluation.
These are automated VISIBILITY indicators, not a guarantee of being cited/indexed/ranked by any AI answer engine (per the response disclaimer).
Responses can be served from cache (response body carries cached:true).
Cheaper focused sub-checks exist on the same host but are separate endpoints: /aeo/llms ($0.005, llms.txt readiness only) and /aeo/crawlers ($0.005, robots AI-crawler matrix only).
Price $0.02 USDC on Base (eip155:8453); no API key.

Harness note: the qa-pay.mjs Sponge settlement returned a raw 402 without paying; the same Sponge wallet paid_fetch with an explicit protocol:x402 hint settled correctly — this endpoint's x402 quote lives in the base64 'payment-required' response header, not the JSON body.
usage.guide: Run a one-call AI-search / answer-engine-optimization (AEO, aka GEO) audit of a website to decide whether a site is discoverable and citeable by ChatGPT search, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Claude and autonomous agents. Send a GET to https://api.agentstools.dev/aeo/audit with exactly one target as a query param — url (preferred, e.g. url=https://example.com), domain (bare domain), or host (hostname); no request body. name: Agentstools SEO Audit
description: One-call deterministic on-page technical-SEO audit of a single web page: fetches the page (following redirects, reading response headers) and runs 24 mechanical rules across six weighted categories, returning a 0-100 score, letter grade, per-rule pass/warn/fail checklist with evidence and concrete fixes, plus an indexability-critical flag. Pay-per-call x402.

backends.inputSchema: GET query params (supply exactly one target): url (string — full target page URL to audit, path preserved, e.g. https://example.com/pricing; PREFERRED), OR domain (string — bare domain, audits its homepage, e.g. example.com), OR host (string — a hostname). No request body.

usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON. Headline: score (int 0-100) + grade (letter A-F) + rating; critical (bool) flags a page that cannot rank with critical_reasons[]. summary{rules_total:24, rules_evaluated, pass, warn, fail, na} counts outcomes. categories[] carries the six weighted per-category subscores (indexability w30, title_meta w20, headings w15, structured_social w15, images w8, i18n_mobile_crawl w12; each {key, name, weight, subscore, rules_evaluated, rules_total}). fixes[] is the actionable subset (only warn/fail rules) with {id, category, status, severity, issue, why_it_matters, recommendation, evidence}; checklist[] is the full 24-rule ledger with per-rule status ('pass'|'warn'|'fail'|'na') and evidence. page{} reports the fetch (status, final_url, redirect_chain, https, robots_allows); sitemap{found, source}; attribution + disclaimer strings; ts (unix); cached (bool).

A rule with nothing to measure returns status 'na' (e.g. image_alt when the page has no images, canonical_self when no canonical is declared), so rules_evaluated < rules_total and a category subscore can be null.
critical:true means the page cannot rank (noindex, robots-blocked, or non-self canonical); critical_reasons[] lists which. In the verified run critical was false.

Mechanical markup checks only — NOT a content-quality/keyword/E-E-A-T judgement and NOT a ranking or indexation guarantee (per the response disclaimer). Responses can be served from cache (body carries cached:true).
